hints: If you fix the longest side of the triangle, which two other sticks give it the best chance of working and also the biggest perimeter?

Sort sticks. For a chosen longest side, the two next-longest sticks below it are the best partners: if even they cannot beat it, no smaller pair can. Scan from the largest side downward and stop at the first valid triple.

1. Sort the lengths in increasing order.
  2. For i from n - 1 down to 2: let the sides be a[i-2], a[i-1], a[i].
  3. If a[i-2] + a[i-1] > a[i], return their sum.
  4. If no triple works, return 0.

approaches.name: Brute force
approaches.idea: Try every triple of sticks, check the triangle rule, keep the largest perimeter.

approaches.name: Optimal
approaches.idea: Sort, then check consecutive triples from the largest end; the first valid one has the maximum perimeter.

explain: For sticks = [3, 6, 2, 3], sorted is [2, 3, 3, 6]. Try longest side 6 with 3 and 3: 3 + 3 = 6 is not greater than 6, so it fails. Next try 3 with 2 and 3: 2 + 3 > 3 is valid, so we return 8. Why consecutive triples: for longest side a[i], the largest possible sum of the other two is a[i-1] + a[i-2], so if that fails nothing with this longest side works. Equality (like [1, 2, 3]) gives zero area and does not count; sides are at most 106, so the perimeter fits in an int.
recognize: Choose items to maximise a sum under a pairwise inequality → sort, then the best candidates sit next to each other.
